sections.overview: Evergestis pallidata is a crambid moth known as the Purple-backed Cabbageworm. It is recorded in Europe and North America.
sections.identification: Adults span about 24–29 mm and have creamy pale forewings laced with dark-brown markings.
sections.habitat: It occurs in a range of grassland and open habitats in regional records; the sources reviewed do not define a single required habitat.
sections.diet: The larvae eat Brassicaceae, including winter-cress (Barbarea vulgaris). North American records list several additional mustard genera.
sections.behavior: Adults fly at dusk and are attracted to light; caterpillars overwinter in cocoons in the soil.
sections.reproduction: It generally has one generation annually, with adults recorded from late spring through summer; pupation occurs in a cocoon.
sections.ecology: The pale adult wings carry characteristic brown markings. Its larvae share brassica hosts with Evergestis limbata; see that profile.
sections.conservation: Belgian regional records document its presence, but the reviewed sources do not give a global risk category.
